title: Concerning the Sea Giant
text:
⟨p.113⟩
41.
41. Concerning the Tongue 41.
of the seas.
Once again the Illuminator said to his disciples: "After the
Living Spirit had set in order the works and the worlds, he came up;
he stood fast upon this earth; he gave a sign to the King of Glory who
casts the three wheels (in motion); he made the wheels which they... {11}
upward in the upper place of all the regions; he scattered the wind forth
[upon] them; blew upon them; raised them up; washed (them) forth from the earth in the wat-
ers. And the Error and the Answering of the three places-of-deceit — that of
[the water, that of] the Darkness, [and] that of the fire, which had been poured upon him — they drove them away
{12} the seas which exist within their shores
⟨p.114⟩
and the places of deceit. Concerning this: The counsels of the salt sea —
since a saltness and a bitterness grew through the casting-forth of the
purification of the three places of deceit. When the Father of
Life came, as he was about (to go) upward in his going to the Height, he cast
the wheel of the stars; he washed it forth; he expelled forth from it
the entire {0} that was within it; he cast it down to the great
sea which is within in the manner {1} of the four. Now he, this Error —
{2} dragon — by the casting-forth from the wheel was cast down
and was mingled inward with the counsels of the sea. His
enthumesis alone gathered him within; she gathered him to his fellows in
this manner. She established him; she ripened him. †ⲉⲓ . ⲉ{3}
the boundary of the sea — with the seal of moments {4}
sealed within it; the seal of days {5}
years; the character of the stars and the zodiac-signs {6}
which came to be from them. They cast it forth from their inner-part;
they cast it to the sea as an icon, with the seals and the faces and the
teachings and the counsels of {7}, sealed in the body
of that boundary. Since it is their entire equipment — therefore
each star that divides, each zodiac-sign that goes
around — there is one who moves it, there is one who establishes it. They
cast it to the sea in this manner, like a cloud
pouring out a downpour into the midst of the sea. He was rained down
after him entirely, through the energeia of the powers and the {8}
steersmanship of the angels. He was driven down to the firmness, the {9}
they established it upon, in the {10} of the cosmos. And she {11}
herself, the sea, became to him {12} as one who {13}
acts as Chief-Image-Painter for him and as Chief-Architect. She painted
him in a likeness different from the other equipment of the bodies
of the sea.
This work being likened in the manner of a
craftsman who carries the molds of coinages of holokoti-
noi (gold solidi) and casts them to the fire, fashioning them into one
icon of the many seals and the many forms — completed
forth, that they may become one body, one {14}
⟨p.115⟩
Thus also is this prow of the sea, which they fashioned itself
—self; they brought it forth in the power of the desire that is in it,
out of many teachings and many counsels{0}, reckoned
to the residue of the wheel of the sphere.
The ty{1}pe of the prow they established for three works. The first is that
the sphere shall winn{2}ow them and purify them out of the burden which ex-
ists in {3}it. As they purified the ten firmaments and winn{4}ow-
ed o{5}ut the burden of the three places of dispersion, in the same manner also
is this — that they made the sphere — that she may winnow herself, {6}puri-
fy-{7} from the burden and the Error that is in her.
The second: that he gives a fastening and a guard to the wheel
and to the zodiac-signs that are bound in it, so that the time, indeed, when they
shall desire to go up to the upper place — again the prow of
the {8}sea, drawing them down in the manner of an i{9}ron fastening,
so that they may have no power to go up. And so that the time when the powers
of the wheel shall take counsel for a work of guile and come to their
heart to come down to the earth, they shall not be able to come down because of
this peg fastened into the wheel which is upon the kar{10} of the
firmaments. The one (reason) is this; but the other on account of her
watchers, the unsleeping ones, who are placed upon her, sifting her at every moment.
{11}The third work: that the {12}wind, the water, and the fire that gush forth from
the {13}encompassing of the sea, {14}and the rivers that flow over the face of
the {15}eart-h, pouring out into the {16}sea, and the abiding-rains that come do-
{17}wnward, and the Error{18} and the metarrismos (transformation) that comes
do{19}wn upon her — th{20}at sea shall serve as the pandocheion (all-receiver)
{21}and the gathering-place inward of all these things.
All the power and the li-
{22}fe that comes down to the sea. And in the breath which the prow
{23}of the sea shall blow forth and draw it to itself, the sea reaching
